options.settle: I want to settle for good
options.family: I want to join my family

pathfinder.resultLead: Based on your answers, start with:

tips.french: Speaking French is a real asset: Express Entry gives extra points for strong French, and Mobilité Francophone opens work permits outside Québec.
tips.english: Bilingual profiles score higher. Adding French to your English could boost your chances significantly.
tips.learning: Plan your language test early: TEF/TCF Canada for French, IELTS/CELPIP for English. Results drive most pathways.
tips.degree: Your diploma counts: we'll help you get it assessed (ECA) so it earns you points.
tips.bac: A Canadian college or university program can be a great first step — and may lead to a post-graduation work permit.
tips.trade: Skilled trades are in demand in Canada — your vocational training may open specific programs.
tips.visit: Visitor files are judged on your ties at home: stable job, family and funds. We'll help you document them.
tips.family: Sponsorship is filed by your family member in Canada — we prepare your side of the file in Algeria.

glossary.title: Canada's immigration words, decoded.
glossary.lead: CAQ, CRS, LMIA… The acronyms that confuse everyone, explained in one line.
glossary.empty: No term found. Ask us during your consultation!

terms.name: Acknowledgement of Receipt
terms.def: Confirmation from IRCC that your application was received and processing has started.

terms.name: Québec's immigration portal
terms.def: The Québec government platform where skilled workers submit an expression of interest to immigrate to Québec.

terms.name: Fingerprints & photo
terms.def: Fingerprints and a photo taken at an official Visa Application Centre (VAC); required for most visa and permit applications.

terms.name: Québec Acceptance Certificate
terms.def: A document issued by Québec that you need before applying for a study permit to study there.

terms.name: Canadian Language Benchmarks
terms.def: The scale that converts your test scores (IELTS, CELPIP, TEF, TCF…) into a level from 1 to 12.

terms.name: Comprehensive Ranking System
terms.def: The points system (out of 1,200) that ranks Express Entry candidates by age, education, language and experience.

terms.name: Québec Selection Certificate
terms.def: Proof that Québec has selected you as an immigrant, before the federal permanent residence application.

terms.name: Designated Learning Institution
terms.def: A school approved to host international students. Your school must be a DLI for you to get a study permit.

terms.name: Educational Credential Assessment
terms.def: A report (e.g. from WES) confirming your Algerian diploma is valid and equivalent to a Canadian one.

terms.name: Federal skilled immigration system
terms.def: IRCC's online system for skilled-worker permanent residence: the best-ranked profiles are invited to apply.

terms.name: Global Case Management System notes
terms.def: The officer's internal notes on your file. Requesting them is the best way to understand a refusal.

terms.name: English language test
terms.def: An English test accepted by IRCC — the General Training version for immigration.

terms.name: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
terms.def: The Government of Canada department that decides on visas, permits and permanent residence.

terms.name: Labour Market Impact Assessment
terms.def: An approval an employer may need to show that hiring a foreign worker won't hurt the Canadian job market.

terms.name: Letter of Acceptance
terms.def: The official admission letter from your Canadian school, needed for the study permit.

terms.name: Francophone mobility program
terms.def: A work permit stream for French speakers with a job offer outside Québec — no LMIA needed.

terms.name: National Occupational Classification
terms.def: Canada's job classification. Your occupation's NOC code and TEER level shape your eligibility.

terms.name: Provincial Attestation Letter
terms.def: A letter from the province confirming your place under the study permit cap; required for most new students.

terms.name: Post-Graduation Work Permit
terms.def: An open work permit that may let eligible graduates of Canadian programs work after their studies.

terms.name: Provincial Nominee Program
terms.def: Each province can nominate immigrants who match its own labour needs.

terms.name: Permanent Residence
terms.def: The status that lets you live, work and study anywhere in Canada — and later apply for citizenship.

terms.name: Financial evidence
terms.def: Bank statements and documents showing you can support yourself (and your family) in Canada.

terms.name: Parents & grandparents visa
terms.def: A long-term visitor visa letting parents and grandparents of Canadians stay up to 5 years per visit.

terms.name: French language tests
terms.def: TEF Canada and TCF Canada: French tests accepted by IRCC and Québec. A strong score is a major asset.

terms.name: Temporary Resident Visa
terms.def: The visa Algerian citizens need to travel to Canada as visitors, students or workers.

faq.title: Questions we hear every day.
faq.more: Another question? Ask us on WhatsApp.

items.q: Is Canadex part of the Canadian government?
items.a: No. Canadex is an independent consulting office in Algeria. Decisions are made only by IRCC and the Canadian authorities, and government fees are always paid directly to them.
Nobody can honestly guarantee a visa. What we guarantee is a complete, coherent and well-documented file that gives you the best possible chance.

items.q: What should I bring to my first appointment?
items.a: Your passport, diplomas and transcripts, CV, and any language test results or previous visa decisions. Copies are fine for the first meeting.

items.q: Do I need to speak French or English?
items.a: For most study, work and immigration programs, yes — and speaking both is a strong advantage. We'll tell you which test to take and the level to aim for.

items.q: Can I book for a family member?
items.a: Yes. Enter their name and your phone number, and mention it in the notes. Families planning to move together can come to the same appointment.

items.q: How do I cancel or change my appointment?
items.a: Call us or message us on WhatsApp with your reference number, ideally 24 hours in advance so someone else can take the slot.
